title: Process pack
description: A set of business processes — the L1/L2/L3 hierarchy — and the components each one uses. Unlike a scan manifest, which is derived from code and covers one repository, a pack is authored by people and spans every repository a process runs through. A pack NEVER creates a component: it only references components that a scan already established. A reference to something that does not exist is reported as a finding, because it means either the scan missed it or this document is stale — and both are worth knowing.

promptVersion.description: Version of the authoring prompt that produced this pack, when one did. Copy it verbatim from the prompt.

pack.description: Stable id for this pack, lowercase. The unit of re-ingest: loading a pack replaces every process it previously contributed and touches nothing else. Split packs by domain or owning team, e.g. 'trading', 'onboarding'.

name.description: Human-readable name for the pack, e.g. 'Trading processes'.

description.description: What this pack covers, and just as usefully what it does not.

authoredAt.description: UTC timestamp when the pack was written or last revised, ISO 8601.

producer.description: Who or what wrote this pack. Ingest uses it to decide trust and precedence.

kind.description: 'human' for hand-authored, 'claude' for an LLM draft, 'import' for a conversion from an existing document such as a Confluence page or a mermaid diagram.

tool.description: Converter and version, when kind is 'import'.

source.description: Default provenance for every process in the pack. A process may override it with its own `source`.

processes.description: Every process in the pack, as a FLAT list. The hierarchy is carried by `code`, not by nesting — do not nest children inside parents.

code.description: The process number as people say it out loud: '2', '2.6', '2.6.13'. This is the identifier and it carries the whole hierarchy — the number of segments is the level (1, 2 or 3) and the parent is the code with its last segment removed, so '2.6.13' is a level 3 whose parent is '2.6'. Every code except a level 1 must have its parent present somewhere in the estate, in this pack or an already-loaded one. Segments are positive integers with no leading zeros. Codes are stable: people cite them in tickets and documents, so renumbering is a real cost — pick a number and keep it.

nodeId.description: A component id exactly as the topology holds it: 'svc:order-service', 'topic:orders.placed.v1', 'db:postgres/orders', 'cache:redis/session', 'api:pricing-service/GET /v1/rates/{}', 'contract:com.meridian.events.OrderPlaced', 'ext:stripe'. Never invent one — if the component you mean is not in the map, reference it anyway and let the finding surface; do not guess at a different id that happens to exist.

source.description: Where this knowledge came from. Process facts are asserted by people, not derived from code, so they carry attribution rather than the file-and-line evidence a scan manifest carries. Do not fabricate a code citation for a process.

kind.description: What sort of source this is.

url.description: Link to the document, diagram or ticket.

title.description: Its title, so the reference survives a dead link.

owner.description: The person or team who confirmed this is accurate.

asOf.description: When it was last confirmed accurate, YYYY-MM-DD. A process nobody has confirmed in a year is worth knowing about.

name.description: The process title, as a thing the business does: 'Place an order', not 'Order service flow'. Keep it short enough to read in a tree.

description.description: What this process is and when it runs, in plain language a new joiner would understand. At level 1 describe the outcome for the customer or the business; at level 3 describe the actual work. Do not restate the title.

owner.description: The team accountable for this process.

trigger.description: What starts it — a customer action, a schedule, an upstream event. Most useful at the leaf.

outcome.description: What is true once it has finished. Most useful at the leaf.

touches.description: Components this process uses, for a process whose steps are not written yet or whose use of a component does not belong to any one step. A parent's component usage is DERIVED by rolling up its children, so do not repeat a child's components here — list only what this level adds.

steps.description: The ordered work, for a LEAF process only. A process that has children must not have steps: the children are its detail. Steps are where the business process meets the architecture, so bind each one to the component or the interaction it actually uses.

seq.description: Position in the process, from 1. Must be unique within the process. Gaps are allowed so a step can be inserted later without renumbering.

name.description: What happens, as an action: 'Reserve the funds', not 'Fund reservation'.

description.description: What this step actually does and why, including anything a reader would otherwise get wrong — retries, idempotency, what happens when it fails.

actor.description: Who or what performs the step, when it is not the service in `node` — a customer, an operator, a scheduled job, an external provider.

node.description: The component this step happens at or to — usually the service doing the work.

interaction.description: The relationship this step travels over, when it crosses a boundary: a Kafka publish, an HTTP call, a database write.

optional.description: True when the step only runs in some cases; explain when in `description`.

notes.description: Anything that does not fit elsewhere: known issues, planned changes, why it is done this odd way.

interaction.description: A relationship in the topology, described the way a person can write it. Ingest resolves it to the edge the scan found, by the same from|kind|to key the scan used — you never write an edge id by hand. `from` is ALWAYS the service, exactly as in a scan manifest; `kind` carries the direction, so a step where a service consumes an event is still from the service to the topic.

from.description: Always the service, never the other end.

kind.description: Same set a scan manifest uses; the two must match exactly or the interaction will not resolve.

to.description: The other end: the topic, database, cache, endpoint or contract.
